**ASSESSMENT 3** 

**AI Procurement Request Copilot** 

Build a small, reliable AI product \- then prove which architecture you would ship. 

**01 Client challenge** 

**THE SITUATION** 

Employees request new software and services. Procurement must check existing tools, team budget, vendor status,  security/privacy requirements and approval rules. Build an AI-powered internal product that gathers evidence and  recommends the next action \- while keeping sensitive decisions with humans. 

**STARTER PACK PROVIDED** 

**DATA** 

Employees \+ budgets \+ software catalog  \+ vendors \+ purchase history \+ requests   
**POLICY** 

Procurement rules \+ approval thresholds  \+ security / privacy requirements   
**MOCK SERVICE** 

Vendor / security status endpoint for tool based retrieval 

**STARTER PACK Download from Google Drive** | drive.google.com/file/d/1rFJsf-VQK5fyQ9qzDjsw2tR0bACQujkA **NOTE** The starter code is a scaffold. If you encounter issues in it, you are expected to diagnose and fix them as part of the  assignment.

**04 Architecture experiment** 

Build A first. Then implement a lightweight B and compare. Maximum recommended: 2 agents. ![][image2]

| EVALUATE BOTH ARCHITECTURES  • Correct recommendation / next action  • Evidence is grounded in tool results  • Policy \+ deterministic rules are followed  • Escalation / human review is correct  • Latency \+ LLM/tool call count | EXPECT EDGE CASES  • Incomplete / ambiguous request  • Existing tool already solves the need  • Conflicting or expired vendor information  • Security-sensitive request or approval threshold  • Prompt injection inside business data  • Tool / API unavailable |
| :---- | :---- |

**FINAL QUESTION** 

**Which architecture would you ship \- and why?** 

Use your evaluation evidence. A simpler system that performs as well or better is a stronger answer than unnecessary  orchestration. UI polish and agent count do not earn extra marks by themselves.
